meta.title: DREA: Decoupled Reasoning and Exploration Agents for Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection
meta.subtitle: Decoupled Architecture with High-Capacity Planner, Lightweight Read-Only Explorer & LLM-as-Judge Lucky Hit Evaluation

views.label: 1. Dataset & Local Workspace
views.note: Phase 1: Ingest 100 RepoPairBench function pairs, local codebase snapshots, and ground-truth CVE/CWE/patch diff specifications.

views.label: 2. Decoupled Planner & Explorer Loop
views.note: Phase 2: Planner (high-capacity LLM) formulates hypotheses and delegates safe read-only queries to Explorer (lightweight LLM).

views.label: 3. Evidence Synthesis & Verdict
views.note: Phase 3: Aggregate Caller/Callee context and Taint paths; Planner synthesizes evidence into XML verdict and rationale.

views.label: 4. LLM-as-Judge Evaluation
views.note: Phase 4: Independent LLM arbitrator evaluates True Positive rationales against ground-truth CVEs and patch diffs.

views.label: 5. Lucky Hits Diagnosis & Performance
views.note: Phase 5: Separate True Positives into True Understanding vs Lucky Hits (26-55%) and compute Pair-Correctness.

cards.title: 1. RepoPairBench & Repository-Level Challenges
items: 1.1. Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection requires understanding full project context: inter-procedural callers, callees, configurations, and data flows rather than examining isolated functions.
1.2. The RepoPairBench-100 benchmark standardizes 100 paired Python functions before and after vulnerability fixes (pre/post-fix), explicitly linked to real CVEs, CWE classes, and commit diffs.
1.3. Local repository snapshots reconstruct entire project filesystems, enabling autonomous agents to read directory hierarchies and source files without overwhelming context windows.
1.4. Enforces the strict Pair-Correctness metric: models must correctly classify both the vulnerable pre-fix version (VULNERABLE) and the patched post-fix version (SECURE) for a pair.

cards.title: 2. Decoupled Multi-Agent Architecture (DREA)
items: 2.1. Clean functional decoupling: The Planner Agent concentrates on high-level security reasoning, while the Explorer Agent specializes strictly in read-only repository navigation.
2.2. The Planner Agent leverages frontier LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) managing hypothesis trees and structured tasks via write_todos (TodoListMiddleware) and Memory Checkpointer.
2.3. The Explorer Agent runs on lightweight models within a sandboxed Virtual Filesystem strictly limited to safe read-only operations: ls, glob, grep, and read_file.
2.4. Tight iterative feedback loop: Planner formulates security hypotheses and delegates inspection -> Explorer collects code evidence -> Planner refines beliefs until conclusive proof is reached.

cards.title: 3. Hypothesis Formulation & Structured Verdicts
items: 3.1. Rigorous scientific methodology: A VULNERABLE verdict requires concrete exploitability proof; a SECURE verdict requires verified defensive evidence.
3.2. Taint & Data-Flow Analysis: Traces Caller hierarchies to find untrusted user-controlled input sources and Callee chains to locate dangerous execution sinks.
3.3. Trigger Path verification: Confirms whether an external attacker controls critical arguments and whether existing validation filters sufficiently prevent vulnerability triggering.
3.4. Standardized XML Output: Mandates explicit <security_assessment> tags, detailed <vulnerability> descriptions (CWE, location, root cause), <trigger_path> traces, and supporting <evidence>.

cards.title: 4. Reasoning Evaluation & The Lucky Hit Phenomenon
items: 4.1. Core empirical insight: Standard binary accuracy heavily overestimates LLM capability; 26% to 55% of True Positive predictions are actually Lucky Hits (correct label, flawed rationale).
4.2. LLM-as-Judge Protocol: An independent evaluator model scrutinizes True Positive reasoning chains against ground-truth CVE descriptions, CWE classifications, and patch diffs.
4.3. Disentangling True Positives: Categorizes results into True Understanding (TU - genuine grasp of root causes) vs. Lucky Hits (LH - spurious guessing or hallucinated mechanisms).

4.4. Comparison against 3 Baselines: Function-only (single function), Whole-file (entire source file), and Single-agent (monolithic LLM); DREA achieves superior Pair-Correctness and reasoning fidelity.
